summary: Scans a directory for files matching an extension filter and appends each hit to a caller-owned linked list. Initializes an iterator state struct (AllocateStructWithDefaultValues), starts file enumeration with sub_565F80(lpFileName, 0, a3, 0), then loops DirectoryEntryIterator until no entry remains. Each iteration allocates an 8-byte node (OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(8), initialized {0, -1}), copies the filename via StringCopyWithBufferRealloc, allocates a 12-byte list entry (initialized {node, 0, 1}) and appends it to the list anchored on this: head this[0], tail this[1], cursor this[2], count this[3]++. The loop breaks when LinkedListNodePeek reports no further entry, and LinkedListDestructorWithChildCleanup tears down the iterator before returning.

operations.description: AllocateStructWithDefaultValues(v9): allocate/initialize the directory iterator state struct on the stack.
sub_565F80(lpFileName, 0, a3, 0): initialize file enumeration over the given directory with the extension filter carried by arguments a3.
Loop over DirectoryEntryIterator(v9); the loop continues while the iterator yields a next matching entry and exits when it yields none.
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(8): allocate an 8-byte node for the current directory entry.
Initialize the node: first dword set to 0, second dword set to -1.
StringCopyWithBufferRealloc(i): copy the iterator's current filename into the node with buffer reallocation as needed.
OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper(12): allocate a 12-byte list entry linking to the node.
Initialize the list entry: first dword points to the node, second dword set to 0, third byte set to 1.

Append the entry to the caller's list: if head this[0] is set, link the old tail (this[1]+4) to the new entry; otherwise set head this[0] and cursor this[2] to it; always update tail this[1] to the new entry and increment count this[3].
LinkedListNodePeek(v9): if no further directory entry is pending, break out of the iteration loop.
LinkedListDestructorWithChildCleanup(v9): destroy the iterator's internal list and child allocations.
Return the result of the iterator cleanup call.
